messages:
incident-bot: PAGER - P1: Elevated 5xx rate for api.redwood.com observed via EU Cloudflare POPs. Symptoms: 525 SSL handshake failures + increased DNS lookup errors. Affected: hosted API (generation, embeddings, streaming). Alert link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/7890 :rotating_light:

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare status: Investigating - geo-DNS & POP routing anomalies in EU region. https://cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/xyz

alice.ops: ack, i'm on it. seeing spike from 09:18Z -> current. 5xx ~ 38% for eu-west prefix.

erin-oncall: i'm the current oncall, jumping in. quick checks: traceroute from eu probe shows routing to a few CF IPs that then return `525`. full client errors in logs are `tls: handshake failure` and `connection reset by peer`. starting deeper checks.

ben-sre: checking our edge health panels — origin is fine (latency/CPU normal). ingress TLS cert still valid, keychain fine. this smells like CF edge -> origin handshake or CF doing partial failover. pulling CF edge logs now.

claire-platform: also seeing an uptick in auth failures for some EU requests: token exchange returns 502 in a subset. unclear if upstream auth provider (okta) is implicated or just failing after handshake. capturing sample request ids: rq_7e3a..

kim-support: field reports: some EU customers report reconnects and streaming disconnects. tickets opening. marking support priority high and adding customers to status page list.

ben-sre: curl/openssl test from ci-eu host (public CF IP observed in traces):
```
openssl s_client -connect 172.65.32.14:443 -servername api.redwood.com
CONNECTED(00000003)
140503... error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
---
no peer certificate available
```
This is CF edge failing TLS negotiation with our origin or presenting no cert to clients in some flows.

alice.ops: i ran `kubectl get secret -n ingress tls-secret -o yaml` — cert rotation happened 3d ago, expires next year. ingress logs show Keep-Alive keep working. not seeing server-side rejects.

cloudflare-status-bot: Update: Cloudflare engineering acknowledges regional DNS resolver throttling + POP routing inconsistencies in EU. They are rolling mitigations. ETA unknown.

ben-sre: options: 1) wait for CF full mitigation (their engineering is on it), 2) change DNS to bypass problematic CF geo-DNS routing (route EU traffic to a backup static set of A records/backup POPs), 3) reduce TLS negotiation surface (disable TLS 1.3/early data) — but 3 is unlikely to help if CF isn't handing certs. We should prepare failover plan #2 now.

ryan-product: customers > SLO impacted, we need quick failover if it reduces impact. approve plan 2 if low risk.

claire-platform: if we do plan 2 we need to ensure CDN bypass won't leak internal endpoints and origin can tolerate traffic. Do we have a direct EU origin behind LB that can take traffic?

alice.ops: yes — we have eu-origin-{a,b}.redwood-internal.net in the private pool. currently traffic goes via CF CNAME -> CF POP -> origin. we can add a short TTL CNAME (30s) to point api-eu.direct.redwood.net (LB) which will send traffic to eu origins. this requires a Route53 change and update to public LB listeners to accept client SNI host `api.redwood.com`. Need deploy-bot to update LB cert if required.

deploy-bot: can do an LB switch if given control-plane thumbs up. will queue change and need 2 approvals.

ben-sre: i'm going to open a Route53 change batch and hold in pending. tagging CF support thread and asking for correlation id from CF engineering so they can exclude our failover testing.

cloudflare-status-bot: CF: We have identified a resolver throttle in multiple EU PoPs causing inconsistent resolution for some customers and an edge routing rebuild for a small percentage of requests. Workaround: customers can switch to static records or use direct origin until the regional fix completes.

erin-oncall: doing the DNS failover now. Change details: route53 change to add CNAME api.redwood.com -> api-eu-direct.redwood.net (TTL 30s) for EU A/B pools. Command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://failover-eu.json` — inside failover file we set weighted routing to prefer direct LB. Executing in 3..2..1

alice.ops: change submitted, change ID: C12345678. propagate TTL 30s. monitoring.

ben-sre: Cloudflare notified of our planned change. waiting for partial propagation. watching error rate.

~5 minutes later~

erin-oncall: metrics update: 5xx drops from 38% -> 6% for EU after DNS shift. streaming reconnects reduced. A small percentage (~2%) of legacy clients still hit edge where CF cached route persists.

kim-support: customer impact reduced; updating status page with note: "Partial mitigation: traffic rerouted to direct EU LB while Cloudflare resolves geo-DNS issue. Some legacy sessions may still see errors."

cloudflare-status-bot: CF: mitigation in progress; we see reduced anomaly after customers shift to static records. root cause under investigation (resolver throttling + POP routing rebuild).

claire-platform: continue watching for origin load — direct LB now seeing ~15% increased CPU on eu-origins, within capacity. autoscale groups warmed up.

ben-sre: confirming error budgets: SLO breach likely for the minute window; notify eng leadership and comms for affected paying customers.

ryan-product: please prepare a short customer note and a followup postmortem. escalate to enterprise ops for any SLA credits.

deploy-bot: rolling back no code; infra change only. no further deploys during incident.

cloudflare-status-bot: Update: Cloudflare has deployed a regional fix to resolver clusters in EU. They recommend customers revert static DNS once their fix fully propagates.

erin-oncall: leaving direct route in place for now. plan: keep failover active for 30m, then coordinate revert during low traf window once CF confirms stable for 30m. handing oncall to ben-sre in 30m for followup monitoring.

ben-sre: taking handoff. summary: P1 caused by Cloudflare EU resolver throttling -> intermittent DNS and POP routing leading to TLS handshake failures (525) for fraction of EU traffic. Mitigated by routing EU traffic to direct LB via Route53 CNAME failover. CF working on root-cause. Post-incident actions: 1) update runbook with clearer failover steps, 2) confirm origin LB TLS acceptance of direct SNI hosts, 3) add synthetic probes to detect CF geo-dns anomalies sooner.

kim-support: created customer list and sent preliminary notification. drafting public status update. will attach incident timeline.

alice.ops: collecting logs/traces for postmortem. saving sample request ids, CF edge ids, resolver ids.

ryan-product: thanks team. low-churn ask: let's ensure enterprise customer tickets prioritized next.

ben-sre: closing thread for active mitigation. will reopen if CF regression occurs. final note: incident start ~09:18Z, failover initiated ~09:25Z, partial mitigation visible ~09:30Z, CF reported regional fix ~09:42Z, we will schedule postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:
